title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-02-01
lineage: SBD > MSR > C > DAT > CD > EAC > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with an uneven early mix captures a ragged‑but‑right 1970 show highlighted by The Other One → Lovelight, China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, Black Peter and High Time.
ai_review.review: The performance is solid – the band plays with conviction despite the after‑effects of the New Orleans bust. Highlights include a monster The Other One → Lovelight stretch, a buttery China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider jam, and strong renditions of Black Peter and High Time. The SBD mix is high on Bob early on and low on drums, but it settles later, making the show enjoyable for fans who appreciate raw 1970 energy.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently 4‑star reviews praise the musical performance and only note mix issues; strong song highlights drive a high rating despite uneven recording balance.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Bob Weir dominates the right channel early, making drums inaudible and Jerry/Phil low. Mix improves after Bear's solo; overall clarity is acceptable but uneven.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Show is a bit ragged with some tuning and stage banter, but transitions (China→Rider, The Other One→Lovelight) are strong and keep the momentum flowing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar audible throughout; great tone on Cold Rain ending and solid presence after mix settles.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is low early but becomes more present later in the show, especially during I Know You Rider.
band_member_comments.Bob: Dominates the right channel early; his playing is crystal clear (both good and bad notes) making him a focal point for fans.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum level is low at the start, improving later; the drum segment is described as a bit long‑winded.
